t: France’s North American empire, reaching from the St Lawrence through the Great Lakes and the Mississippi to the Gulf of Mexico.
It rested on the fur trade and Native alliances, but had only about 70,000 settlers in Canada by 1760.
Britain conquered it in the Seven Years War, yet its language, law and Catholicism survive in Quebec today.
dyk: Between 1663 and 1673 about 800 young women, the filles du roi, were sent from France at royal expense to marry settlers, and millions of French Canadians descend from them.
ev: Jacques Cartier claims the Gaspé Peninsula for France
Louis XIV makes New France a royal province
La Salle reaches the mouth of the Mississippi and claims Louisiana
The Great Peace of Montreal ends war with the Iroquois Confederacy
Quebec falls after the Battle of the Plains of Abraham
The Treaty of Paris cedes Canada to Britain
